text:
katie.l: Heads up — saw a 3x read-latency spike on local NVMe in eu-west2 during the 02:00 batch window. GPU attach queue stalled for ~6m, several pods pending.

mike.b: Ugh. Any signs of SMART errors or firmware churn?

katie.l: No SMART flaps. Drives mostly healthy. Pattern looks like sustained tiny-random reads causing IOPS to saturate. Tail latency up to ~45ms.

janitor-bot: ALERT eu-west2-nvme: read-latency > 30ms (hostpool-8a), 02:11-02:18 UTC. Affected: gpu-provisioner, scratch-cleaner.

yusuf: Can you paste the iostat/top output? Curious about queue depth + util.

katie.l: pasted snippet from the affected host: ```avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           1.0    0.0    2.4    58.3    0.0   38.3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await  w_await  aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1         1200     30  51200    800    0     0     40.2     1.2    1.8   98.6
```

sanjay: 1200 r/s small reads -> that's the issue. %util at 98.6 means IO queueing. Which service is producing the tiny reads?

katie.l: traced it to scratch-cleaner and a set of training checkpoints being scanned by our background indexer. Both hit small 4k reads repeatedly.

mike.b: Are those reads random or sequential? If random, NVMe suffers on small IO. Could we throttle cleaner or batch indexer?

katie.l: Random. I pushed a temporary throttle on scratch-cleaner to 50% concurrency at 02:25 and saw tail latency reduce back to ~2-3ms and GPU attaches recovered.

yusuf: Good mitigation. Two follow-ups: 1) can we add an IOPS cap on scratch-cleaner systemd/cgroup for eu-west2 pool? 2) investigate caching for indexer to reduce backend reads.

sanjay: +1 on cgroup cap. Also consider changing readahead/batching for the indexer (read-ahead 64 vs default). Might convert random 4k to more sequential 32k windows.

mike.b: For long-term, we should detect these microbursts earlier and circuit-break GPU provisioning when local pool saturates. Smart routing to warm spare nodes in other regions could avoid failed attaches.

katie.l: Filed infra ticket: INFRA-4247 to add iops-cgroup + indexer-batching change + alert tuning. Will attach trace logs.

janitor-bot: NOTE INFRA-4247 created by katie.l (priority: P2).

yusuf: Cost question — if we shift cleaner to S3-backed cleanup tasks (more network egress + object ops), will it increase bill vs local wear? Need rough numbers.

mike.b: Quick calc: moving heavy reads off local reduces NVMe wear (long-term replacement cost) and frees capacity; S3 GET cost ~ $0.0004 per 1k objects read (rough). If cleaner hits 50M ops/month, that's ~$20k/mo vs a few k for additional drive replacements. We'll quantify.

sanjay: Also consider a hybrid: sample-first on local metadata, then batch object reads to S3 for heavy scanning. Keeps GPU attach reliability and limits local IO.

katie.l: Immediate action items: (a) enable cgroup iops cap on eu-west2 scratch pool (rolled at 03:00) (b) add temporary alert for nvme read-latency > 25ms (c) plan indexer batching change. I'll coordinate rollout windows with platform.

mike.b: Thanks. If anyone oncall sees repeat at scale, ping @sanjay and I'll escalate to cross-region fallback. :thumbsup:

katie.l: Closing loop: after cap rolled, 02:30-03:00 window looked stable. We'll keep monitoring and post postmortem if it happens again. :eyes:
